#2752. How the Denver Broncos can beat the Carolina Panthers

The Denver Broncos sit atop the AFC West with a 6-2 record. On Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers who are 3-4 and in first place of the NFC South for their Week 9 matchup. Denver has momentum entering the game being winners of four in a row, whilst Carolina has dropped back-to-back games. Here are three ways I think the Broncos can earn their seventh victory of the season.

Last season, Denver had an effective running game in the first half of the season. Unfortunately, it tapered off greatly after J.K. Dobbins was injured. This year, Denver has experienced the opposite. It's been a relatively slow start for them establishing the run, but injuries have played a part in that this year too.

While Denver's current stable of backs isn't completely 100-percent health-wise, I think there is a huge opportunity here to revitalize their run game on Sunday. Why? Because the Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the National Football League.

It's clearly a giant weakness for the Carolina. They are allowing nearly 5 yards per carry. Moreover, they've been dreadful in four of seven games with respect to rushing yards. They gave up 291 on the ground to the Chicago Bears, 258 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 157 to the Atlanta Falcons, and 132 to the Cleveland Browns.

I'd love to see a healthy dose of Jonah Coleman in this game. The rookie running back has looked good in his limited opportunities and deserves a majority of the carriers moving forward. It's a road game, so dictating the pace of it will be essential, and enforcing a consistent rushing attack is key to that.

Whether or not the Broncos will be buyers at the trade deadline remains to be seen. However, the more opportunities Coleman gets, the easier the evaluation process for him as a player gets. And in turn, would help answer whether or not the franchise needs to trade off quality draft capital to add to the room prior to November 10th.

Believe it or not, the Panthers enter Sunday's matchup as a Top 10 offense in the National Football League. Quarterback Bryce Young has played a big part in that. He has thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions thus far in his fourth season leading their offense.

Young sported a few hot games to start the season. However, he has struggled recently. The former top-pick has 3 interceptions and just 2 touchdowns in their back-to-back losses. His accuracy has also experienced a big drop-off—completing less than 57-percent of passes the past three games.

In 2025, Young was one of the least sacked quarterbacks in the NFL with just 27. In seven games, he has already been sacked 23 times. The crazy part? Eleven of those have come in the past two games alone. Knowing that, this seems like a prime week for Denver's defensive trenches to rev up the pass rush. If they can rattle and get after Young early and often, they'll have a great shot at winning.

The Broncos are a 6-2 football team despite struggling in many key areas. One major issue for them since Week 1 has been their inability to convert on third down. The Broncos are now dead last in the NFL with under a 30-percent conversion rate.

It's true Denver has faced some really good defenses. However, that isn't an excuse for their poor play in this regard. This is arguably the biggest area the Broncos have to improve upon as they gear up for Sunday's matchup—as well as the second half stretch of the season after their bye week.

The Panthers have a bottom 5 third down defense in the NFL. Opposing teams are converting 46-percent of third downs against them each week. Head Coach Sean Payton, quarterback Bo Nix, and the rest of the offense need to find a way to sustain drives and move the field on third down.

Last season, Courtland Sutton was the go-to guy if Denver needed to move the chains. Perhaps this weekend the Broncos make the savvy veteran their main target in the passing attack when they need a big play. He has been clutch through his career in that aspect. If not, who on offense can step up and be that player?

#2751. Spurs hold off Mavs behind Wembanyama’s historic night

The San Antonio Spurs concluded their homestand in thrilling fashion on Wednesday night, holding off a furious second half rally by the Dallas Mavericks to earn the 112-111 victory at the Frost Bank Center behind a historic and career night from Victor Wembanyama.

The victory is the sixth straight for San Antonio, who defeated Dallas for the second time this season.

Wembanyama was fired up from pre-game introductions, pumping his team up as he went through the high-five line. From the opening tip, he was aggressive inside the paint and getting to the free throw line. He scored eight of the Spurs' first 10 points and would finish the first quarter with 15 points.

The second quarter saw both teams go on a pair of runs. With the Spurs leading 48-39, Mavericks coach Dusty May called timeout and following that, Dallas went on a 7-0 run to cut San Antonio's nine point lead down to two points. Meanwhile, later in the period, the Spurs would close the second quarter on 19-3 run to take the 68-51 advantage into the second half.

Wembanyama finished the first half with 29 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks. The one area where Wemby struggled? His three-point shooting, just going 1-for-8 on the night.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said after the game. "I mean, my shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is here. I can do it, but I can be much better if my shots fell."

Both teams had a slow start to the second half, but it was Dallas that looked like a team that got a grilling at the break. The Mavericks were much more aggressive to begin the third quarter, led by Kyrie Irving and Naji Marshall. At one point, Julian Champagnie left Marshall open for a corner three. That left Spurs coach Mitch Johnson furious as he called timeout and let his team know just how frustrated he was with their effort.

The Spurs responded out of the timeout by building the lead back to 13 points, but Dallas would win the third quarter 27-22 and that set up a thrilling finish in the final 12 minutes. The Mavericks opened the fourth quarter by outscoring San Antonio 12-4, all but erasing their 19-point deficit. The final 8:45 saw both teams go back and forth exchanging the lead, but this Wembanyama would not allow the Spurs to lose on this night.

San Antonio got their star the ball at every chance down the court over the final three minutes. He had two putbacks in the final 2:39, but went just 1-for-4 from the free throw line, causing anxiety for many inside the arena. With the Spurs clinging to the 112-111 lead, Dallas had one final chance. Irving missed a contested 15-foot, turnaround jumper with three seconds remaining thanks to some great defense from De'Aaron Fox and the Spurs held on.

Wemby finished with career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds along with eight blocks.

"I think he's settled into the season like we all have," Coach Johnson said of his star player after the game. "We're almost 10 games in. It takes a minute to get in that flow, we had to just got to a good spot in terms of team [needing] to get where their feet were. Team has potential. We're starting to play the brand of basketball we should."

Dallas was led by Irving's 29 points, seven rebounds, and five assists. Marshall added 22, while PJ Washington chipped in 21 and Cooper Flagg added 19 points for the Mavericks, who fell to 4-4 on the season.

Dylan Harper, who finished with 21 points, said postgame that he looked up to Irving growing up and to play against him is incredible, but beating him meant more.

"It was good to get the win over him today for sure," he said after the game.

In addition to Wemby's career highs, the victory for the Spurs was also the 100th in Coach Mitch Johnson's career. According to Spurs socials, Wemby presented Johnson with the game ball in the locker room after the game.

Devin Vassell and Champagnie went a combined 0-for-14 on the night. Coach Johnson said after the game he doesn't believe we'll see a game where that happens again this season.

San Antonio's bench struggled on the night, scoring just 10 points compared to 38 points from Dallas' second unit.

The Spurs were ice cold (no pun intended on throwback night) from beyond the arc, shooting just 13 percent and going 5-for-36. That will and should change as the season goes on.

#2750. George Karlaftis quotes a classic Disney movie in a message to players

Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis spoke with reporters on Wednesday. He referenced a classic Disney movie in a message to his younger teammates to keep them motivated through this season's uncertainty.

"Both with R Mason (Thomas) and with Pete (Woods). I had this conversation before the season. We were having conversations from time to time in season. Like, look, guys, I was a first-round pick, and whatever success I've had, I was a first-round pick, and I didn't have a full sack until after Thanksgiving," said Karlaftis. "Yeah, there's ebbs and flows, right? You doubt yourself. You see yourself do something good on the tape, and it really makes a man out of you. Really, I mean, to be quite honest, you have to produce at the end of the day."

Karlaftis had two tackles, three passes defensed, one tackle-for-loss, one quarterback hit, one forced fumble, and a sack in last Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos.

"So with those guys, just always keep at it. Just like what it's like in Finding Nemo, and Dory says, 'Just keep swimming, man, just keep swimming'," said Karlaftis. "Those guys love football, you know. Those guys love football, and when they just keep at it, keep chopping wood, just keep improving, keep finding those little details in your game, maybe that pressure becomes a sack, or maybe that missed tackle becomes a TFL (Tackle For Loss). So it's really about finding the little things, because I I can remember myself vividly going through hours after games or after a bad practice, just figuring it out, because it's a long process and it takes everything out of you."

Karlaftis' three passes defensed moved his total to a league-high seven for the year among all defensive linemen. He also sacked Broncos quarterback Bo Nix for a 5-yard loss, bringing his season total to 2 sacks.

#2748. 2026 NHL free agent tracker: Patrick Kane returns to Blackhawks on two-year contract

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

NHL free agency has slowed down in late July, but some notable names are still coming off the board. Most notably, Patrick Kane is returning to the Chicago Blackhawks on a two-year contract worth $16 million, the team announced on Thursday.

Already a Chicago legend and future Hall of Famer, Kane won three Stanley Cups and a slew of individual awards with the franchise that selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in 2007. Kane's first stint with the Blackhawks lasted 16 seasons, and he piled up 446 goals and 779 assists in 1,161 games. Kane ranks inside the top five of just about every statistical category in franchise history, and he will get the chance to keep climbing those lists over the next two years.

The Blackhawks sent Kane to the New York Rangers at the 2023 NHL trade deadline, and he played just 19 regular season games there before hitting free agency the next summer. Hip surgery delayed Kane's decision until November of that year, but he ultimately landed with the Detroit Red Wings, where he's spent the last three seasons.

Last season was Kane's best with Detroit, and it proved that he still had some gas left in the tank, at least offensively. Kane posted 16 goals and 41 assists in 67 games -- with 19 of those points coming on the power play.

In his second stint with the Blackhawks, Kane will add another level of playmaking to the power play, and he should strengthen a top six forward group that's bereft of proven talent. Kane will also be an excellent mentor and sounding board for fellow No. 1 overall pick, Connor Bedard, who is set to miss the first month of the season after undergoing shoulder surgery.

Kane isn't the player he once was, but he'll give Chicago a bit more pop at the top of the lineup, and his first game back in a Blackhawks jersey will be a huge night for the city.

#2744. How the Chicago Bears Are Controlling the Clock This Season

One of the more notable aspects of the Chicago Bears' performance this season has been their ability to control the clock. The Bears are averaging 35:26 in time of possession, putting together extended drives, consistently moving the chains, and giving opposing offenses fewer opportunities with the football.

On Monday night, the Bears put together a 17-play, 80-yard opening drive against the Seattle Seahawks that took 8:32 off the clock.

Caleb Williams noted that sustaining drives was something the offense spent time working on during training camp and OTAs.

"We do these long-drive drills in training camp and OTAs that you hate, that you dread at the end of practice," he said. "They show up in big moments for us."

And while the Bears' offense is well-prepared to execute those extended drives, Johnson's priority remains making the most of each possession rather than focusing on how long a drive lasts.

"It's not something we stress," Johnson said. "We really talk more about getting explosive plays. I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown. But the ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I think that's something that good offenses show that they can do."

Johnson also pointed out that long drives leave little room for mistakes, since one misstep can bring an otherwise promising possession to an end.

"I prefer some more explosive plays be mixed in there, just so it takes the onus off just a little bit," Johnson explained. "It feels like you've got to be perfect throughout those long drives, and one mistake could derail you."

One factor contributing to the Bears' success in controlling possession has been their performance on third down on both sides of the ball.

The Bears convert 44.3% of their third downs, the fifth-best mark in the NFL, while their defense ranks No. 1 in the league, allowing conversions on just 23.8% of third downs.

What's made Chicago particularly dangerous on third down is that the offense hasn't just been converting in those situations. Some of the Bears' most explosive plays this season have come when they've needed to move the chains.Williams connects with Odunze on a spectacular third-down throw vs. Patriots

Kalif Raymond breaks loose for a big gain to set up Bears touchdown vs. Seahawks

Luther Burden III comes up big with a 24-yard touchdown on 3rd and 17

Time of possession might not be a statistic Ben Johnson puts much emphasis on, but the Bears' ability to win on third down and sustain drives allows Chicago to control the clock and dictate the tempo of games is certainly part of what makes this team special.

#2743. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2741. Joe Mazzulla has faith Queta, Robinson will find their footing with Boston Celtics

With a few notable exceptions, the Boston Celtics big men have not had the best start to the 2026-27 NBA regular season. And given Mitchell Robinson won a title with the New York Knicks this summer and Neemias Queta is seeing his role change with the arrival of Robinson, both have something they can point to explain if not excuse it.

But Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla is not too worried about that dynamic, instead trusting his centers to sort out their roles sooner than later. "The fives are the most important position that we have on both ends of the floor because of their ability to navigate our defense and the offensive's ... way they play directly has a positive impact on the other guys," said Mazzulla on Wednesday (Nov. 4) night. "And so there's a relationship aspect there that's really important. Everyone on our team knows that position is extremely important."

"They have to be one of the smartest positions, and they do a great job of that. I think what's not being valued is (Mitchell Robinson's) ability to help everyone else," he added. "His individual rebounding might be down a little bit, but what's not down is how he's positively impacting the other guys. (How he is) getting cleaner shots for guys, keeping matchups so that teams can't cross-match and they have to stay on him because of his size and getting there."

"There's a lot of stuff that's not measured that he's doing good," said Mazzulla. "The easiest measurable thing is the one thing that he's been great at his whole career, which is rebounding."

"And some of that (is that) he has to get better at it. But he's doing stuff for the other guys that's making it look easier for them, and that's a product of him. And you can't measure that, so that's on us to be able to show that stuff in film and measure that stuff."

#2740. Watch Klay Thompson hit overtime game-winner to beat Clippers, cap 30-point night

Inglewood, Calif. — These are the moments Klay Thompson lives for: His team down two, the game on the line and he rises for the last shot.

"I can't lie to you, felt really good," Thompson said.

That shot capped off Thompson's first 30-point game since he was still a Warrior in 2024. The Warriors needed every one of those points — and that game-winning final shot — to beat the Clippers 117-116 in overtime at the Intuit Dome.

When asked about that shot, Heat coach Erik Spoelstra pointed out the screen Bam Adebayo set on the baseline to free Thompson for the game-winning corner 3.

"[Thompson] had great timing on that, and then Bam had one heck of a screen..." Erik Spoelstra said. "It was fitting to be able to finish the game that way."

"Screeners don't usually get a lot of credit, but that's probably my best screen, for sure..." said Adebayo, who led the Heat with 35 points. "I just had to make sure I got him open. The guy is one of the greatest shooters in league history. So my biggest thing was to make sure he got open."

Thompson has had an up-and-down start to his first season in Miami, with his defense being the real cause for concern. However, both Spoelstra and Thompson said the conditioning and extra work Thompson has put in — and continues to put in — is what paid off on the court.

"I feel amazing. I haven't felt this good in a long time," said Thompson, who has pushed through injuries in recent years. "No pain in my lower Limbs, and I'm so grateful to be here. I mean, they hold me accountable, the training staff and the coaching staff, and I feel amazing. I haven't felt this good to start a season in years."

Giannis Antetokounmpo added 27 points for the Heat, plus hit some clutch free throws. Darius Garland led the Clippers with 26 points.

Next up for Thompson and the Heat: A trip to the Bay Area to take on Klay's former team, the Golden State Warriors. A team with a pretty good shooter of their own — but Thompson is in a groove and had more than one white-hot night in the Chase Center.

#2738. Bears’ Jeffrey Simmons trade forces the NFC North’s hand

The NFC North is stacked with all four teams currently having a winning record.

This division is likely going to be a battle until the final week of the season. Monday night, the three other teams in the division got to see how the Chicago Bears are going to be set up for the stretch run and it had to terrify them all.

In their first game since their blockbuster trade for star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons, the Bears manhandled the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on the road. Simmons was a monster in his Chicago debut, making the team feel pretty good about their decision to send two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for their defense changer.

Now, the other three teams have to respond by making big moves of their own. They might not all match the Simmons' deal in terms of star power, but aggression is needed around the NFC North.

Here is a move each of the 6-2 Bears' rivals can make before Tuesday's trade deadline:

The Lions are 5-2. They could use some help on defense, though. Linebacker is an obvious concern with the injuries to Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder. So a pursuit of a tackle machine like Jordyn Brooks of the Miami Dolphins could make sense. But we're going to look at the secondary for the Lions. They have had a need since they released 2024 first-round pick Terrion Arnold in the summer because of legal reasons.

So, we're going to pair the Lions with Philadelphia Eagles' cornerback Riq Woolen. He may be the best cornerback on the market and he could make an impact with Detroit. He won a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks last year, so he knows how to play in important games. Woolen is 6-foot-4 and is a matchup concern. Plus, he is a free agent after the season, so he could come at a reasonable price. It wouldn't be a Simmons-like get, but Woolen would make the Lions better and that's the whole point of adding at the trade deadline.

The 5-3 Packers have been rumored to be interested in Indianapolis Colts' running back Jonathan Taylor. That's understandable with what is going on with running back Josh Jacobs. But acquiring Taylor might be complicated for the Packers. So, we're going elsewhere for their deadline addition.

It may not be as sexy, but Green Bay needs an upgrade on the offensive line. So, we're looking at the Eagles again. Howie Roseman is always open for business. So, the Packers should push for guard Landon Dickerson. He is a solid sixth-year pro and he would be an upgrade for a solid offense that needs help up front. Dickerson, 28, will be a free agent in 2028. But a third-day draft pick could do the trick for Green Bay. Again, this isn't an earth-rattling acquisition, but the Packers would be better with Dickerson.

No, we're not sending Kirk Cousins to the Vikings. That would be too pricey for the value.

Taylor is the call here. He's what the 6-1 Vikings need.

Taylor could change the Minnesota offense and make life easier for quarterback Kyler Murray. An offense featuring wide receiver Justin Jefferson and a tailback like Taylor would be dangerous. Coupled with the Vikings' defense, this team would be a legitimate Super Bowl threat and they would put pressure on the surging Bears.

The price tag may be multiple premium draft picks, but it would be worth it for the Vikings to make this deal.

#2737. Commanders' defense has historic night in Week 8

Despite Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne not being in the game, the Washington Commanders defense had a historic night against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football with a season-high in pressures and one of the best performances using the blitz of any defense in the NFL this season.

Washington held Philadelphia to just 10 points, the Eagles' second-fewest points in a game this season. That was also the first time this season the Commanders have held an opponent under 20 points. Their defense finished the game with a total of five sacks and held quarterback Tanner McKee to just 212 passing yards. They also contained running back Saquon Barkley, who only had 30 rushing yards.

The defense's performance allowed Washington to run away with this game in the second half as the Eagles did not score after the first quarter. In fact, Philadelphia did not have a drive that lasted more than 60 yards until the end of the game, when they had a 34-yard completion as time expired.

Washington's defense will need to be just as dominant this coming Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams are dealing with injury issues of their own, especially on defense, which should open things up for the Commanders offense. However, Washington's secondary will still have to contend with All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua, who has 19 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns in the past two games.

#2735. Career-best Wembanyama display seals Spurs win

Victor Wembanyama sank the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday.

The French star, whose previous best was 50 points in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to also claim 24 rebounds and eight blocks.

The 22-year-old is the first player in 52 years with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game.

He also became the fifth player since 1982 to register at least 50 points and 20 rebounds as San Antonio improved their record to 6-2.

Wembanyama reached half-time with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals, before the Spurs held off a second-half rally by Dallas, who were led by 29 points from Kyrie Irving.

"I haven't been feeling great lately," said Wembanyama. "I've been sick for a while.

"Today I felt like I got my legs back, so it should be more like this more often."

Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash.

Brown (30 points) and Embiid (26) led a balanced offensive performance as Philadelphia saw all five starters reach double figures, with LeBron James claiming a double-double of 13 points and 10 rebounds.

The 76ers now have the NBA's best record at 8-1 after bringing in Brown and James in the off-season.

"It's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature," said James. "We'll just continue to buy into what we want to do. We got a good team."

The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings 116-103 with Luka Doncic scoring a game-high 40 points to reach 308 for the season.

The Slovenian star became the first player to pass 300 in his first eight games of a season since Michael Jordan (303) in 1988-89.

Doncic was also involved in an incident which led to a fan being removed after throwing the ball at an official, which struck her as she was signalling a Lakers possession.

Meanwhile, London-born OG Anunoby scored 18 points for the New York Knicks as the reigning champions enjoyed their biggest win of the season, beating the Chicago Bulls 135-105 to improve to 4-4.

#2734. Buccaneers, Bears: Week 9 game preview

Anyone watch Monday Night Football? Wow, the Bears look good. Ben Johnson, Caleb Williams, and their Chicago Bears seem like they are on a collision course for a deep playoff run in 2026. So yes, the Bears are hot— Steaming, but so are the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay is coming off two-straight wins, three of their last four and has seemingly found their new formula for offensive success. Will those good vibes and momentum carry over into the Chicago night on Sunday Night Football?

"Battles are won in the trenches, in the grit and grime of courageous determination."

The Chicago Bears are no joke and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will need to be all the way buttoned up to be able to stay with Chicago in this game. The Bears have a lot of things going for them in 2026, but their most recent addition may be the scariest. Chicago's highly publicized trade for Jeffery Simmons opened some eyes when they made it. For those who haven't seen may Titans' games over the years, Monday night may have opened some more— Simmons is in the elite class of football players in the NFL and after spending years on a losing team, he looks motivated and rejuvenated. The trade for Simmons was an all-in move, the kind of move teams make when they have one goal on their mind— The Bears are a Super Bowl or bust team.

The trade paid immediate dividends, Simmons' first game with Chicago was a watch what I can do performance as he snared a team-leading six tackles (two for a loss) and a sack. For the Buccaneers, this game will be the game where their offensive line needs to prove the last two weeks true.

Tampa's season began horrifically, 0-4, a quarterback injury, and more importantly for the sake of this discussion, an offensive line that was woeful. Tampa Bay's offensive line came into the season projected to be one of the strongest units on the team, perhaps in the league, depending on who you asked. Through the first four games, the Buccaneers allowed 20 sacks. Baker Mayfield spent most of those first four games running in circles behind the line of scrimmage like Fran Tarkenton, until he ran himself into an injury. In the four since, Tampa's only surrendered seven sacks with five of the seven coming against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Tampa Bay will be and should be the underdog on Sunday. If there is any chance that an upset is in the cards they will need to protect their quarterback. Baker Mayfield is going to have to attempt more than three passes in this game to lead the team to victory and he will need to be upright to do so. Chicago has an absolute game-wrecker on their defense, he will make his plays— The Bucs can't expect to wipe Jeffery Simmons out of the game, however, they cannot allow the game to devolve into what fans saw earlier in the season from this offensive line, Baker Mayfield, and the passing game.

"You can't stop him, you can only hope to contain him."

Caleb Williams might not be a truly great quarterback, though he does seem to be enroute to that status in short order, but he is a truly special athlete. No, he isn't running 4.2 40's or leaping 13' in a broad jump but he is as all around dynamic as they come. One of the issues Tampa Bay might have is Williams simply does not throw interceptions. Caleb has missed some time this year, but he has only thrown one interception— Last year, just seven. Williams' lack of interceptions isn't even a Ben Johnson related statistic because dating back two years ago, pre their union, Williams tossed just six while throwing 20 touchdowns for a better than 3:1 touchdown to interception ratio. In his career (three years), Williams has thrown less interceptions than Baker Mayfield did in 2024—Turnovers may be off the table.

Another key issue that Caleb Williams presents is his elite management of the pocket. Williams is not a runner, but he is quite mobile. He has a phenomenal ability to majestically glide up, back, or out of the pocket towards free space and away from danger. Todd Bowles and the Buccaneers' defense will need to work tirelessly to mitigate that on Sunday night. Williams will dagger the Bucs with big plays off script if they let him.

Bowles and the Bucs have been somewhat of mixed bag against mobile quarterbacks, different matchups bringing about different results, but Caleb Williams will represent a very unique challenge. Williams is not just looking to move around the pocket to buy time to throw— He isn't just looking break out of the pocket so that he heave the ball down field on a broken play— He won't be looking to run outside of contain so that he can scramble for yards to move the chains— Caleb Williams will be looking to do any and all of the above. He is special and he has proven that he can do each and every one of those things on any given play— Meaning, the Buccaneers must be dialed into the details on their rushes, sound in their tackling, and if they are caught lacking and take even just one snap off Williams could gash them for a game changing play.

Todd Bowles' defense has been reliably solid in 2026, as of late they've been exemplary. Sunday night's game against Chicago will be a true test. Caleb Williams has the ability to put a defense on a poster, he and Ben Johnson have left a decent amount of carnation in their wake. Can Tampa Bay contain Caleb Williams and stay off his highlight reel?

#2733. Seahawks QB Drew Lock will look to dominate the Cardinals once again

The Seattle Seahawks announced that starting quarterback Sam Darnold is dealing with quad and rib injuries. It'll be Darnold's second stint on the sidelines this season due to injury. Backup Drew Lock will start against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 on Sunday.

Lock looked extremely comfortable operating Brian Fleury's offense in that game. The Cardinals defense hasn't gotten better since then, and they are rumored to trade veterans like Budda Baker and Josh Sweat before the deadline. Lock should toy with the Cardinals in Week 9.

#2732. Rockets drop one to Timberwolves, fall 117-107

The ghosts of last season popped up in last night's 117-107 Houston Rockets loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Up until last night, Houston seemed to have largely fixed many of the problems they had last season. Had they been right all along about what Fred VanVleet would mean to this team?

Well, last night, even with VanVleet, the Rockets suffered through some poor fourth quarter offensive execution, which was a hallmark of last year's team (blowing leads), and gave up a 10-2 run midway through the fourth after leading by a couple and finished in a 10-point defeat.

The Wolves were without Anthony Edwards and Terrence Shannon Jr., so they were shorthanded, while the Rockets mostly were not (missing only Steven Adams), but it was still Houston's fourth quarter that cost them the game, when they turned the ball over four times and shot just 7-for-16 in the final frame, while simultaneously letting the Wolves finish strong, shooting 13-for-21 in the fourth.

The Rockets were led by Alperen Sengun, who racked up a triple double, going for 17 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists, but he shot just 5-for-15 from the field. They also got 21 points from Kevin Durant and 18 from Fred VanVleet, but overall, the Rockets shot just 43 percent from the field while allowing Minny to go off for 53 percent. Houston was also outrebounded and outplayed in just about every category.

The Wolves were led by Ayo Dosunmu, who put in 21 points, while Lamelo Ball scored 20, including 12 in the decisive fourth quarter, while Jonathan Kuminga had 16, including a three-pointer and a tip-in down the stretch that helped win the game for the Wolves.

That was a home game for the Rockets, so you hate to see old habits pop back up again, but you're going to have nights like these over an 82-game season. Keeping them at once in a while and not 20 blown fourth-quarter leads like last year is the key. Things had been better to start year, and it's certainly not anywhere close to panic time, but it was a little disheartening to see the Rockets of old pop back up last night. I guess number one in the power rankings comes with expectations?

The Rockets will be back in action Saturday night against the Phoenix Suns. That game is in Phoenix and has an 8pm start.

#2731. Who is Joe Fagnano? Meet undrafted rookie QB making first start for Ravens

Joe Fagnano's tenure as an NFL starter might be an abridged one.

With the Baltimore Ravens losing starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley to likely season-ending injuries, Fagnano was called upon to fill in for Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

But the undrafted rookie from UConn might not hold the reins to the offense much longer than that.

On Wednesday, the Ravens were finalizing a trade with the Arizona Cardinals to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The deal still leaves Fagnano in line to be the first-stringer for Thursday. But with an extended break before the Week 10 "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, Brissett is the logical candidate to take over for that tilt − and the rest of the season.

Still, Fagnano could play a significant role in shaping a turbulent campaign for Baltimore.

After beginning his career as a walk-on at Maine and then transferring to UConn after four years, Fagnano enjoyed a remarkably efficient season as a seventh-year senior in 2025, when he threw for 3,448 yards and 28 touchdowns with just one interception.

That was enough to earn him invites to the East-West Shrine Bowl and NFL Scouting Combine. In the 2026 NFL Draft, however, Fagnano was not selected.

Though he joined the Ravens shortly after, his signing was overshadowed by Diego Pavia, the Heisman Trophy runner-up who also joined the team as a free agent. Pavia, however, was waived by the Ravens in late July. Fagnano would go on to lead all quarterbacks in passing yards in the preseason en route to securing a spot on the 53-man roster.

His inaugural pro season figured to be spent primarily watching Jackson, the two-time NFL MVP, and possibly Huntley, who has established himself as one of the league's more reliable backups. That left Fagnano to make his debut in suboptimal circumstances. In his first pro action, Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception.

Even though the 6-foot-3, 226-pound passer suffered an ankle injury and now will face a stifling Jaguars defense, Baltimore is still keeping its faith in Fagnano.

#2730. Deniz Undav plays down Germany call-up hopes amid goal drought

VfB Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav is not expecting to be called up for Germany's upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

The 30-year-old was asked whether he was hoping for a call-up in the mixed zone after Stuttgart's 2-0 defeat to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“Not at all. Without goals, it's difficult to get into the squad,” he replied, adding that he had yet to receive any indication that he could be selected.

Undav has found the net just twice in 14 appearances in all competitions this season and is still waiting for his first Bundesliga goal of the 2026/27 campaign.

“I have no comment on why there have been so few goals. I genuinely don't know. I'm trying to work on it, but it's just not happening. Somehow, I can't seem to get going,” Undav said.

Having left Undav out of his first squad, Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp is set to announce his second selection on Thursday.

#2729. Bears' Jeffery Simmons will be ready for Good, Better, Best next time

All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is good at a lot of things, but the "Good, Better, Best" chant was not one of them after the Chicago Bears' 34-17 win against the Seattle Seahawks.

Simmons had not even been with the Bears for a week before Monday night's game against Seattle and head coach Ben Johnson's "Good, Better, Best" postgame chant is unlike anything any other head coach in the NFL does. During the footage of his "Good, Better, Best" after Monday's win, it was clear Simmons did not know the words yet. But he has been studying film on YouTube and promised to be ready for Chicago's next game.

"I definitely been on YouTube trying to figure that, make sure I'm good for next game," Simmons said. "Next game, especially I'm in the camera like that, I know the words. I'll be ready."

Luckily, Simmons has his college teammate, edge rusher Montez Sweat, to help him learn the words. They did a lot of winning together at Mississippi State. Simmons also got to experience a winning culture in his first three years in the NFL during his time with the Tennessee Titans. However, the Titans have not had a winning season since 2021, so this is the first time Simmons has gotten to be part of a winning culture in five years.

"When you winning, great things happen and when you're a part of something like that after a game, you're doing something good and to feel the energy, feel the excitement from everybody in the locker room after a game," Simmons said. "It's great to be a part of."

Chicago is currently heavy favorites over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for their next game on Sunday Night Football. So, barring anything catastrophic, Simmons will get to say the "Good, Better, Best" chant along with the rest of the Bears in the locker room after the game.

#2728. Raiders OL will absolutely have their hands full with 49ers DL

The Las Vegas Raiders ended a four-game losing streak by defeating the New York Jets in Week 8. They'll face a stiff matchup versus the San Francisco 49ers in Week 9. The offensive line will especially have a difficult matchup with the 49ers' defensive line.

It's fair to say the Raiders' offensive line has underperformed this season. The run-game has especially been underwhelming. The Raiders are already on their third starting right guard, with rookie Trey Zuhn receiving the latest opportunity. None of those decisions have been injury related.

The 49ers have registered just 15 sacks in seven games. The advanced metrics indicate they've been better than that. The Raiders have allowed 11 sacks, with only three offenses allowing fewer sacks.

The 49ers' pass-rush-win-rate is 49%, according to ESPN Analytics. That ranks 20th in the league. Meanwhile, the Raiders' pass-blocking-win-rate is 63%, second-best among NFL offensive lines. The 49ers have talented pass rushers such as Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner (recently acquired via trade), Mykel Williams, Keion White, and Romello Height. The matchup won't be straightforward.

Some of the 49ers' pass-rushing metrics will definitely improve now that they've traded for Buckner. Many metrics favor the Raiders' offensive line, but the challenge will be bigger than some realize.

#2727. 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Falcons

The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 victory against the Tennessee Titans, while the Falcons lost 16-0 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a rain-soaked contest.

Even with that loss this past week, the 3-5 Falcons are not a team to take lightly. They have victories over the Packers, Saints, and the 49ers this season. They also have one-score losses against the Steelers, Ravens, and Bears. They will be getting back their best pass rusher, James Pearce Jr., this week also. He is coming off an 8-game suspension he served for violating the NFL's conduct policy.

With the aforementioned Pearce coming off of his suspension, he is listed as the starter at right outside linebacker in the Falcons' 3-4 defense. That means he is likely to face off against Orlando Brown Jr. this week. Brown struggled at times on Sunday when faced off against the speedier pass rush of Jacob Martin. He will see a similar test with the athletic Pearce this week.

Orlando Brown Jr. allowed a season-high 6 pressures versus Tennessee. He was also credited with allowing a sack. Brown will have to play much better this week against Pearce. Last season Pearce produced at an elite level for a rookie. He finished the season with 45 pressures and 10.5 sacks for the Falcons. The Bengals will need to keep Pearce and the rest of a dynamic Falcons pass rush in check this week.

Slowing down Bijan Robinson is going to take a full team effort. While it will be up to everyone to try and limit him this week, I am specifically curious to see how Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., and Jordan Battle play. Those three players have struggled with missed tackles the last couple of seasons. Robinson is one of the most dynamic and elusive running backs in the league. He can make guys look absolutely silly out in space, and that trio will have to play sound football. If they don't, we are going to see them all over the Bijan Robinson highlight reel.

Bijan already has 780 rushing yards on the season. Toss in another 203 receiving yards, and he is about to eclipse 1,000 all-purpose yards already this season. The best running back in the league rushed for over 1,400 yards last season. He also finished the year with over 800 receiving yards. A player who can absolutely put the Falcons team on his back at times.

If the Bengals' effort against the run looks like it did on the long Tony Pollard touchdown run this past week, they are going to be in for a long day in Spain.

I have no idea what the Bengals will plan on doing this week against Kyle Pitts at tight end. While Pitts hasn't had the career many expected, he is still a dynamic receiving threat for the Falcons. Add in the fact that the Bengals cannot stop a tight end at all again this season, and Pitts could be in for a career game this week. The Bengals allowed Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger to grab eight receptions for 112 yards this past week against the Titans.

I am never really sure what their plan for guarding tight ends is on a weekly basis. Jordan Battle made a couple of plays guarding tight ends, but most of the game we were just seeing guys completely wide open down the field at the position. I put it to be determined here because I don't know why they won't give Tacario Davis more of a chance to guard tight ends. I think that role would be DJ Ivey, but he has been thrust into starting at corner after the injury to Jalen Davis.

Regardless of who ends up being responsible for guarding Kyle Pitts this week, I am fully expecting him to put up a hugely productive game.

Neuzil and the rest of the Falcons interior offensive line will be tasked with trying to stop the unstoppable in Bengals defensive tackle Lawrence this week. Lawrence is coming off a week with 7 tackles, a sack, and a fumble recovery. Lawrence is playing at an elite level this season, and now has 24 pressures and 5 sacks through his first 7 games of the year.

Neuzil has allowed just 6 total pressures and 1 sack this season for Atlanta. However, Dexter Lawrence is a completely different animal to face. Neuzil will get help from Matthew Bergeron at left guard and Chris Lindstrom at right guard on Lawrence during this game, as well. Bergeron has allowed just 8 pressures with 0 sacks this season, while Lindstrom has allowed only 6 pressures and 1 sack. That interior offensive line has held up pretty well, but the Bengals are one of the toughest matchups to date for those guys. It should be a really fun matchup throughout the day.

#2726. 3 things from Charlotte's 114-104 defeat to Brooklyn

The Charlotte Hornets dropped their fifth game in a row Wednesday night, losing at the hands of the Brooklyn Nets, who entered the matchup with a 1-6 record. Charlotte's main issues (turnovers, scoring and shooting) came to the forefront once more, as the Hornets lost 114-104. To add injury to insult, second-year forward Kon Knueppel was forced to leave his season debut after six minutes with a leg injury.

Naz Reid led the team in scoring, finishing with 28 points and nine rebounds on 11-for-18 shooting from the field. Grayson Allen finished with 22 points off the bench, 20 of which he scored in the first half. For Brooklyn, Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle combined to score 48 points, with rookie Mikel Brown Jr. chipping in 18 off the bench. Prior to Charlotte's matchup Friday against the Boston Celtics, here are three things to take note of.

Although the Hornets have a couple of players struggling when it comes to turnovers (Naz Reid and Dennis Schroder) and 3-point shooting (Sion James and Schroder), the blame should be spread out pretty evenly, except for maybe Grayson Allen, who's been the team's biggest bright spot early on. Wednesday night against the Nets, eight of 11 players in Charlotte's rotation committed multiple turnovers, including Knueppel, who only played six minutes. The same can be said for the Hornets' shooting struggles, as the majority of the team has struggled from long-distance. Charlotte shot 30% from deep on 40 attempts Wednesday against Brooklyn.

While many expected the Hornets to have a slow start in large part due to injuries or take a step back altogether following the departure of LaMelo Ball, the future of the team appears much more bleak than anticipated. Currently on a five-game losing streak, Charlotte's struggles don't appear to be an overnight fix. With injuries and serviceable veterans who hold solid trade value, things could potentially get worse before they get better.

The Charlotte Hornets haven't lost their identity; they just can't succeed at what made them so successful last year, which you could argue is even worse than losing your identity. Off to a horrendous start offensively to begin the season, the Hornets are faced with the decision of abandoning their 3-point-reliant offense that made them so dynamic a year ago. Currently, the Hornets are 28th in the NBA in 3-point percentage, despite ranking No. 3 in attempts. While they haven't had a large sample size when fully healthy, it may be a while until they are, with Knueppel going down in Wednesday's game. Is Charlotte's current personnel flexible enough for a change in play style? Or will the Hornets become sellers way sooner than ever anticipated?

#2724. Celtics passed their first Jayson Tatum-less test: ‘We believe in our depth’

BOSTON — For the first time this season, the Boston Celtics were without star Jayson Tatum. The team announced his absence Wednesday afternoon, meaning it would have to adjust its approach when hosting the Milwaukee Bucks at TD Garden.

Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla further outlined those adjustments before opening tip.

"The sub pattern is going to be different," Mazzulla said pregame. "The starting lineup's gonna be different. The end-of-quarter lineups are gonna be different because he plays the whole quarter. So we'll play a bunch of different lineups. What doesn't change is the process of how we have to execute on both ends of the floor, but some of the tactical stuff will change."

With Tatum resting, Mazzulla inserted Paul George, Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Neemias Queta and Hugo González into Boston's starting lineup. In the first quarter, George played all 12 minutes, Queta, Mitchell Robinson and Luka Garza rotated through a double-big combination, and Baylor Scheierman played more than half the frame as the Celtics dug deep into their depth.

Boston shuffled through 10 different players in the first quarter alone.

For the rest of the team, the objective was simple.

"Get a win," White said. "It's kind of the thing we always talk about; people in, people not in. We play how we play and just gotta go out there and get a win. Obviously it changes a little bit because JT does a lot for us, but at the end of the day, we believe in our depth, we believe in every person in the locker room, and we just gotta go out there and get a win."

Garza, the team's leader in 3-point makes in Houston (four), picked up right where he left off. Coming off the bench, he knocked down each of his first three 3-pointers to enter halftime as Boston's leading scorer with 11 points. He also grabbed five rebounds, including three on the offensive glass, continuing his early-season emergence as Mr. Reliable in the Celtics' reserve unit.

In the second half, as George and White began to carry the offensive load, Scheierman worked in tandem with Queta to clean up the glass.

The two combined for 15 rebounds in the second half, with Scheierman coming through with the biggest board of the night. He secured an offensive rebound with fewer than three minutes remaining in the fourth quarter before finding a cutting White, who finished the right-handed layup through contact and converted the three-point play at the free-throw line.

That put the Celtics ahead 102-97 with 2:22 left, providing some breathing room after the Bucks erased a 22-point deficit to take their first lead with 6:50 left.

It also helped navigate Pritchard's early departure in the fourth quarter. The Celtics guard suffered an eye injury in the third quarter and was unable to return.

To George, who led Boston with 25 points, it was a good experience to overcome those late-game dramatics without a full-strength crew to help ease the stress.

"Just collectively coming together," George said. "Learning, down the stretch, how to play together in that moment."

In many ways, the Celtics treated the one-win Bucks as a must-win matchup. They approached the night with immediate urgency, and once they slipped, they got back up and responded.

George and the rest of the team shut down Milwaukee's comeback bid quickly, as the Bucks never led by more than a single point. He knocked down a clutch step-back three over Jaime Jaquez Jr. to extend Boston's advantage to 107-99 with 1:22 left. But despite hearing TD Garden's "MVP" chants directed his way, George was quick to credit the victory as a result of a group effort more than anything else.

Everyone pitched in, and the Celtics managed without their superstar forward.

"It was a five-man thing out there where everybody was helping each other, pulling for one another," George explained. "We had to rebound. We had to scratch, claw. It was a physical battle that I thought we collectively [overcame]. We have to do that. We have to come together and play together, and it's just value for us to get those wins. Obviously, we want JT to get his rest in those situations, so we gotta come together and collectively be big in those moments."

#2723. Who is Joe Milton? 5 things to know about Eagles' new starting QB

The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton in hopes of reviving an offense that has struggled through eight games and six consecutive losses. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, Philadelphia will start Milton against the New York Giants on Sunday, replacing Tanner McKee after three consecutive losses, with the former Stanford quarterback directing the offense.

The move comes less than three weeks after the Eagles signed Milton from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, giving the former Tennessee standout an unexpected opportunity to become Philadelphia's third starting quarterback of the season.

Here are five things to know about the Eagles' new starting quarterback.

Milton began his college career at Michigan in 2018 and spent three seasons with the Wolverines before transferring to Tennessee. He initially competed for playing time behind other quarterbacks before earning a start in 2020.

Milton transferred to Tennessee in 2021, where he spent three seasons developing under head coach Josh Heupel.

The change of scenery eventually helped him establish himself as an NFL prospect.

Milton became Tennessee's full-time starting quarterback in 2023, completing 229 of 354 passes for 2,813 yards, 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. He also rushed for 299 yards and seven touchdowns, demonstrating the mobility that makes him an intriguing option for Philadelphia's offense.

The 6-foot-5 quarterback finished the season with 3,112 yards of total offense, helping Tennessee finish the regular season 8-4.

His exceptional arm strength became one of his defining traits during the pre-draft process, though questions about consistency and accuracy contributed to his sixth-round selection.

The Patriots selected Milton with the 193rd overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. He made his regular-season debut against Buffalo in the 2024 season finale, completing 22 of 29 passes for 241 yards and one touchdown while rushing for another score.

New England won 23-16, giving Milton a chance to show his physical tools against NFL competition.

Despite the encouraging performance, the Patriots eventually moved in another direction at quarterback.

New England traded Milton to Dallas during the 2025 offseason, giving him another opportunity to develop behind an established starter. Milton appeared in four games for the Cowboys during the 2025 season, completing 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions.

Dallas eventually moved him to its practice squad, where Philadelphia signed him on Oct. 16. He arrived as the Eagles dealt with uncertainty around Jalen Hurts, whose season was derailed by blood clots.

Milton now has an opportunity to establish himself with an NFC East rival.

Milton brings a different skill set than McKee, particularly with his ability to throw deep passes and extend plays outside the pocket. Those traits could give offensive coordinator Sean Mannion more options for an offense averaging 17.1 points per game.

Philadelphia has struggled to consistently create explosive plays, sustain drives, and establish its running game.

Milton's mobility could help offset some protection issues, while his arm strength creates opportunities to stretch opposing defenses. However, he must also demonstrate improved decision-making and accuracy after receiving limited regular-season opportunities during his first two NFL seasons. The Eagles enter Sunday at 2-6, making Milton's first start with Philadelphia an important audition for a quarterback trying to establish himself as a legitimate NFL starter.

#2720. Another night, another uncoordinated mess in Phoenix

When you're going through it, it feels like absolutely nothing can go right. For every good thing that happens, two bad things seem to follow. In the context of basketball, where five players are supposed to operate as one cohesive unit, that kind of dysfunction becomes maddening to witness.

Wednesday night against the Portland Trail Blazers, the Suns weren't taking baby steps forward. They were performing the old one step forward, two steps back routine, stumbling over their own feet while desperately trying to find some semblance of rhythm. And perhaps that's what this season is ultimately going to be. One long, uncoordinated dance performed by a team that can't seem to get its choreography straight.

A season ago, the Suns established an identity built around toughness, grit, and hustle. This version of the team is developing an entirely different identity, one defined by a perpetual inability to find its rhythm. When the bass finally starts hitting the right notes, the drummer loses the beat. When the lead guitarist finds a groove, the singer comes in wildly off-key. Everybody seems to know the song they're supposed to be playing, yet somehow they're all performing a different version of it. And good luck trying to dance to that mess.

One of the few bright spots early in the season has been the Suns' bench. That second unit has provided energy, production, and occasional stability when the starters have struggled to find their footing. Against Portland, however, that bench completely disappeared.

Phoenix entered the game with legitimate concerns about its size, although the first half offered some encouraging signs. The Suns outrebounded the Trail Blazers 23-19 and were narrowly outscored in the paint, 28-24. There was enough there to suggest they might be able to survive their physical disadvantages. As the game progressed, however, that rebounding advantage dissipated into the dance floor fog, and the rout was underway.

The starting unit actually did a respectable job putting points on the board, combining for 94 points despite shooting 29.6% from beyond the arc. There were offensive contributions to build upon, even if the execution wasn't always pretty.

The bench? If you see them, ask them to report to the scorer's table. Through the first three quarters, Portland's bench outscored Phoenix's reserves 28-11. Seventeen points. That's the difference between having a second unit that can sustain momentum and one that sends the entire operation careening into a ditch.

Therein lies the fundamental problem with these Suns. They cannot seem to fire on all cylinders at the same time. When the starters produce, the bench disappears. When the offense begins to find its footing, the defense forgets how to function. When one part of the team finally discovers the rhythm, another loses the beat entirely.

For one night, you'd love to see everybody playing the same song. Instead, we're watching a band that desperately needs a rehearsal, a conductor, and perhaps a few lessons in basic rhythm. And the dance floor is getting awfully uncomfortable.

Miles Bridges takes down his first Bright Side Baller as a Sun after posting a 21-point, 6-rebound, 3-assist, 4-steal, 1-block stat line against the Warriors on Monday. He took down 72% of the vote, one of the most dominant wins early on this year.

#2719. Illini duo post career nights in season opener

CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Illini defeated Detroit Mercy in an 84-50 in their first showing of the season Wednesday night at State Farm Center. The orange and blue were led by one of the nation's best frontcourts, Cearah Parchment and Berry Wallace, notching a decade-old achievement.

The Illini struggled with turnovers early, 15 of their 18 total coming in the first half. However, Illinois never wavered on the boards, out-rebounding the Titans 25-13 in the first half. Wallace (6) and Parchment (5) led the way across the first two periods, in a game that was still within striking distance for the Titans.

The Illini ultimately pulled away in the second half, outscoring Detroit Mercy 48-18. Parchment and Wallace were Illinois' top rebounders, both finishing with 11 boards. Of Wallace's 11 rebounds, five came on the offensive end, a key part in creating extra possessions for the Illini. The orange and blue ended Wednesday night's matchup with an extremely positive rebound margin, doubling Detroit Mercy, 53-23 on the glass.

A major part in the Illini's victory against Kiefer Haffey's Titans was their relentless attack on the inside. Illinois outscored Detroit Mercy in the paint 38-22 on a solid 45% shooting.

Parchment had a stellar night from the field, shooting 82% on nine makes, only missing both of her three-point attempts. The sophomore standout dazzled Illini fans with a number of crafty post moves to help her squad pull away. Parchment finished the night with 22 points.

Wallace, likewise, showed a real ability to play some bully ball. The All-Big Ten First-Team selection star shot 8—of-16 from the field and also splashed two shots from beyond the arc. Wallace ended the night right behind Parchment with 21 points.

Parchment and Wallace became the first Illini teammates to post 20-point double-doubles in a contest since 2013.

Both players have been garnering national attention ahead of this season. Parchment, who was on the All Big Ten Freshman team last year, was named to the Katrina McClain Power Forward of the Year Watchlist.

Wallace has been named to the Cheryl Miller Small Forward of the Year Watchlist, as well as the Naismith Player of the Year Watchlist, an amazing feat for the junior.

The two Illini stars will continue to feed off each other's incredible versatility and look to make a deep run in the postseason this year.

There's a strategy to NFL Survivor. You could, before Week 1, arrange the teams 1-32 in order of Super Bowl odds and simply go down the list week by week. But you'd run into issues — some obvious, some less so. And even if it went well, by Week 17 or Week 18, you could be playing for a title and have no one better than someone like the Buccaneers or Raiders left available to you. Do I want to write that being strategic explains why I have three losses in eight weeks? Well, yeah. It's not true, but any excuse, you know? But the strategic factor plays in every week. It's not just picking a team that should win; it's picking a team that should win while not burning all your good late-season options. Check out my Week 9 pick for Survivor contests. And while we're here, you can use our NFL Betting Model and our Bet Tracker to make a pick for yourself.

Every week, we have the same process. We eliminate teams in groups until we narrow it down to our real considerations. Start with all 32, whittle it down. And remember — this game is "once you use a team, they're off the board," so it's not always just a matter of taking the team you think will win. There has to be some strategy. I can't pick a team I've picked before, but you might not have tailed me, so previously used teams are eligible until the end.

My favorite category — picks I can't get wrong! If you don't play, you can't win, but also I won't pick you, so woohoo for easy. Pittsburgh Steelers Tennessee Titans That's two off the board.

You can face the worst team in all of football, but if you're the second-worst team, well, I'm still not going to be too excited about selecting you. #2714. Wizards drop measuring stick game against Hawks

Call it a learning experience. An education. School.

The Wizards entered last night's game against the Atlanta Hawks having played the NBA's easiest schedule so far. Their opponents had an average scoring differential of -9.83 per game. The Hawks — a middle-of-the-pack team missing their best player — were a step up.

The Wizards weren't bad in this measuring stick kind of game, but they did get outplayed by a bit. Not every possession, but they got beat to the punch regularly throughout the contest — outshot, out-rebounded, out-competed.

Which is okay for an eighth game of the season after a three-year tank. The Wizards are trying to win this season, and against teams of similar talent level, they'll need to up their level of compete. Games like this one could help them do that — if they seize the opportunity to learn what true NBA competition requires.

The chief area in need of some attention is ending possessions when they get the other team to miss a shot. They entered the game ranked 26th in defensive rebounding percentage and gave up 19 offensive rebounds to a tiny team with two guys 6-9 or taller, one of whom (Asa Newell) hyperextended a toe and missed the second half.

The Wizards get a second crack at the Hawks Friday night in their second NBA Cup game. If Washington wants to contend for something other than the bottom of the play-in this season, they'll need to figure out a way to clean up the defensive boards — at least to some degree. It'd be great if they could force some opponent turnovers too (they're 27th in defensive turnover rate). But first things first — defense in the NBA is mostly about making the other team miss and then getting the rebound. That's where the focus should be.

Bilal Coulibaly doesn't look to be an offensive threat, which ultimately undermines his defensive value because he's a self-check. Chase Hughes and the Monumental broadcast team tried to turn it into a positive (the segment about how trying to win slots young players into their proper roles and now Coulibaly doesn't have to force anything), but…it's basically nonsense. Coulibaly doesn't have to be an alpha scorer, but he does need to be able to take an open three, attack a closeout, or drive competently a few times a game.

An example — in the first quarter, Trae Young passed to Coulibaly — defended by the much smaller and less athletic CJ McCollum — in the dunker spot. Coulibaly gave zero thought to attacking. He just passed it back out to Young. The possession stalled, Young passed it back to Coulibaly at the three-point line, and McCollum stripped him. The lack of aggression converted a clear offensive advantage into a turnover instead of a good shot.

Later in the first quarter, Coulibaly provided a counter-example — he drove right, got a paint touch, collapsed the defense, and kicked it out to Alex Sarr up top. Sarr missed the wide open three, but the point here is the excellent shot created by Coulibaly attacking. Reminder: last season, opposing defenders had trouble staying in front of Coulibaly when he decided to drive, even when they gave him space and dared him to shoot.

The Monumental broadcast never ceases to amuse. At the end of the first half, Chris Miller raved about the Wizards closing on a 9-0 run. It was indeed nice. Worth mention: they still trailed by seven.

Kyshawn George turned in a pretty good game — 25 points on 10-14 shooting along with four rebounds and seven assists. That's the good stuff. He also committed four turnovers and four fouls. I want to believe in him, but he's gotta cut out some of the negatives if he's going to help drive winning.

Anthony Davis scored 26 points on 12-19 shooting, had 10 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 blocks. Of note: zero turnovers, zero fouls.

Below are the four factors that decide wins and losses in basketball — shooting (efg), rebounding (offensive rebounds), ball handling (turnovers), fouling (free throws made).

eFG% (effective field goal percentage, which accounts for the three-point shot)

TOV% (turnover percentage — turnovers divided by possessions)

FTM/FGA (free throws made divided by field goal attempts)

PPA is my overall production metric, which credits players for things they do that help a team win (scoring, rebounding, playmaking, defending) and dings them for things that hurt (missed shots, turnovers, bad defense, fouls).

PPA is a per possession metric designed for larger data sets. In small sample sizes, the numbers can get weird. In PPA, 100 is average, higher is better and replacement level is 45. For a single game, replacement level isn't much use, and I reiterate the caution about small samples sometimes producing weird results.

POSS is the number of possessions each player was on the floor in this game.

ORTG = offensive rating, which is points produced per individual possessions x 100. League average so far this season is listed in the Four Factors table above. Points produced is not the same as points scored. It includes the value of assists and offensive rebounds, as well as sharing credit when receiving an assist.

USG = offensive usage rate. Average is 20%. Median last season was 17.7%.

ORTG and USG are versions of stats created by former Wizards assistant coach Dean Oliver and modified by me. ORTG is an efficiency measure that accounts for the value of shooting, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers. USG includes shooting from the floor and free throw line, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers.

+PTS = "Plus Points" is a measure of the points gained or lost by each player based on their efficiency in this game compared to league average efficiency on the same number of possessions. A player with an offensive rating (points produced per possession x 100) of 100 who uses 20 possessions would produce 20 points. If the league average efficiency is 115, the league — on average — would produced 23.0 points in the same 20 possessions. So, the player in this hypothetical would have a +PTS score of -3.0.

Players are sorted by total production in the game.
